_meta.purpose: T16.7 license-compatibility gate input for in-boundary ML dependencies named in Addendum 7.4a (Whisper, pyannote.audio, openSMILE, HDBSCAN, BERTopic, statsmodels, bocd).
_meta.verification_method: individually web-searched against upstream repo/PyPI metadata; this is a point-in-time snapshot, not a live SBOM run (no network access in the build sandbox to run pip-licenses/syft against an installed environment)
_meta.action_required: wire this gate to a real SBOM tool (pip-licenses / syft / SPDX scanner) in a network-enabled CI job; treat this file as the seed manifest and initial findings, not a substitute for that.
_meta.blocker_status: openSMILE audEERING-NC and bocd UNKNOWN are explicitly identified as unresolved in-boundary blockers

openai-whisper.source: upstream setup.py (license="MIT"), confirmed via repo metadata
openai-whisper.notes: package license only. Whisper's own model weights are separately released by OpenAI; if a different checkpoint/fork is ever substituted, re-verify.

pyannote.audio.notes: package license is MIT, but the pretrained pipelines used at runtime (e.g. pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 on HuggingFace) are gated behind separate HuggingFace user-conditions acceptance -- that's a usage-terms/access issue, not a redistribution-license issue, but worth tracking alongside this gate since it blocks unattended deployment without a one-time manual acceptance step.

hdbscan.source: upstream conda-forge meta.yaml and repo README

bertopic.source: upstream repo PyPI classifiers / packaging metadata

statsmodels.source: well-established upstream license, not independently re-searched this pass

opensmile.source: upstream repo README (audeering/opensmile, audeering/opensmile-python): "source code and binaries are freely available for private, research, and educational use... It is not allowed to use the open-source version of openSMILE for any sort of commercial product... we require you to buy a commercial development license."
opensmile.notes: NOT an OSI open-source license -- source-available with a commercial-use prohibition. This is a business-blocking finding, not a copyleft one: see README.md. Sprint 2 already deploys this for prosody extraction.

bocd.source: no LICENSE clearly published for the specific reference implementation named in the Sprint 5 spec (gwgundersen/bocd); a separately-named, unrelated PyPI package 'pybocd' (different author, different codebase) is GPL-3.0-or-later -- do not conflate the two.
bocd.notes: fails closed pending manual verification. If gwgundersen/bocd is confirmed unlicensed (all-rights-reserved by default), it cannot be used at all without contacting the author; if a differently-licensed reference implementation is substituted, re-verify and update this entry.
